This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there is a graph $H$ with $m$ edges such that in any $2$-colouring of the edges of $H$ there is a monochromatic copy of $G$. 
Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be the union of stars. More precisely, let $F_1=\cup_{i\leq s} K_{1,n_i}$ and $F_2=\cup_{j\leq t} K_{1,m_j}$ with $n_1\geq \cdots \geq n_s\geq 1$ and $m_1\geq \cdots \geq m_t\geq 1$. Prove that\[\hat{R}(F_1,F_2) = \sum_{2\leq k\leq s+t}l_k\]where\[l_k=\max\{n_i+m_j-1 : i+j=k\}.\]
#561: [BEFRS78]
graph theory | 
ramsey theory
Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp [BEFRS78] proved this when all the $n_i$ are identical and all the $m_i$ are identical.
Győri and Schelp [GySc02] proved this when $\binom{l_k}{2}> \sum_{k\leq i\leq s+t}l_i$ for all $2\leq k\leq s+t$. More special cases, including all cases when $s=1$, or $s=2$ and $n_1=n_2$, or all $n_i$ and $m_j$ are odd, or all $n_i$ are an identical odd number and $m_1$ is odd, were proved by Davoodi, Javadi, Kamranian, and Raeisi [DJKR25]. 
This problem is #30 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

 I'll note that this is AI-assisted by the new Qwen 3.8 Max (I quite like this model, though it tends to make up theorems). The comment is written by me with some polishing by 3.8 Max, it is only a partial lower bound.
Let\[
n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_s\ge1,\qquad m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_t\ge1,
\]and\[
F_1=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^sK_{1,n_i},\qquad
F_2=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^tK_{1,m_j}.
\]As usual, put\[
\ell_k=\max_{i+j=k}(n_i+m_j-1)\qquad(2\le k\le s+t).
\]Also let\[
\varepsilon(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
1,&a,b\text{ are both odd, or }\min\{a,b\}=1,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]and\[
\eta_k=
1-\max_{\substack{i+j=k\\n_i+m_j-1=\ell_k}}
\varepsilon(n_i,m_j)
\qquad(2\le k<s+t).
\]Thus \(\eta_k=0\) exactly when some maximizing pair on the \(k\)-th diagonal has both entries odd, or one of them is \(1\).
We prove the following lower bound\[
\widehat R(F_1,F_2)\ge
\sum_{k=2}^{s+t}\ell_k-\sum_{k=2}^{s+t-1}\eta_k.
\]Write\[
A_i=\bigsqcup_{r=i}^sK_{1,n_r},\qquad
B_j=\bigsqcup_{r=j}^tK_{1,m_r},
\]and say that \(P_k(G)\) holds if\[
G\to(A_i,B_j)\qquad\text{for every }i+j=k.
\]First, for every \(v\in V(G)\),\[
P_k(G)\Longrightarrow P_{k+1}(G-v).
\]To see this, fix \(i+j=k+1\). Suppose \(i>1\), and start with an \((A_i,B_j)\)-free coloring of \(G-v\). Color all edges at \(v\) red. Since \(P_k(G)\) holds, there is a red \(A_{i-1}\). Delete the star of this copy containing \(v\), or any one of its stars if none contains \(v\). What remains lies in \(G-v\) and contains a red \(A_i\), because\[
n_{i-1}\ge n_i\ge\cdots\ge n_s.
\]This is a contradiction. The case \(i=1\) is the same with red and blue interchanged, using \(B_{j-1}\).
We also need the following standard splitting fact:\[
\Delta(H)\le a+b-3+\varepsilon(a,b)
\Longrightarrow
E(H)=R\sqcup B,\qquad
\Delta(R)\le a-1,\quad\Delta(B)\le b-1.
\]If \(\varepsilon(a,b)=0\), Vizing gives at most \(a+b-2\) matching classes; take \(a-1\) red and \(b-1\) blue. If \(\min\{a,b\}=1\), just use the other color. Finally, suppose \(a,b\) are odd and put \(D=a+b-2\). Take a disjoint copy \(H'\cong H\), and for each \(x\in V(H)\) add \(D-d_H(x)\) parallel edges from \(x\) to its copy \(x'\). This gives a \(D\)-regular multigraph. Split a \(2\)-factorization into \((a-1)/2\) red factors and \((b-1)/2\) blue factors, and restrict back to \(H\).
Now take \(G\to(F_1,F_2)\). Put \(G_2=G\), and for \(2\le k<s+t\) choose a maximum-degree vertex \(v_k\in V(G_k)\) and let\[
G_{k+1}=G_k-v_k.
\]The deletion observation gives \(P_k(G_k)\) for every \(k\).
Fix \(2\le k<s+t\), and choose a maximizing pair \(i+j=k\) with\[
\varepsilon(n_i,m_j)=1-\eta_k.
\]If\[
\Delta(G_k)\le\ell_k-\eta_k-1
=n_i+m_j-3+\varepsilon(n_i,m_j),
\]the splitting fact gives a coloring of \(G_k\) with no red \(K_{1,n_i}\) and no blue \(K_{1,m_j}\). Hence there is no red \(A_i\) and no blue \(B_j\), contradicting \(P_k(G_k)\). Therefore\[
\Delta(G_k)\ge\ell_k-\eta_k.
\]It remains to deal with the last graph. Write \(e=e(G_{s+t})\). If\[
e\le n_s+m_t-2,
\]color \(\min\{e,n_s-1\}\) edges red and all the others blue. There are then at most \(n_s-1\) red edges and at most \(m_t-1\) blue edges, so neither required star appears. Hence\[
e(G_{s+t})\ge n_s+m_t-1=\ell_{s+t}.
\]Finally,\[
\begin{aligned}
e(G)
&=\sum_{k=2}^{s+t-1}d_{G_k}(v_k)+e(G_{s+t})\\
&\ge\sum_{k=2}^{s+t-1}(\ell_k-\eta_k)+\ell_{s+t}\\
&=\sum_{k=2}^{s+t}\ell_k-\sum_{k=2}^{s+t-1}\eta_k.
\end{aligned}
\]Taking the minimum over all \(G\to(F_1,F_2)\) proves the bound.

A partial proof 
claimed by tienxion (using OpenAI Codex (GPT-6), including parallel research agents).
 Summary:
 We prove the conjectured size Ramsey formula for pairs of star forests whose diagonal maxima satisfy explicit local gap conditions. The proof builds on earlier simultaneous-tail lower bound by controlling the maximum-degree vertices in equality cases and applying Fournier’s edge-colouring theorem. This gives exact values for additional families, including families where it improves the earlier lower bound by arbitrarily many edges, but does not fully resolve this problem.
 Notes:
 This is a partial result. The simultaneous-tail framework, good-diagonal definition, and parity-dependent deficit bound are due to Ricky Cipollini (rickyc), whose 6 August 2026 contribution is explicitly cited in the manuscript. The additional step is equality-host degree control under local gap conditions. AI assistance was used in developing and writing the draft; the submitting human reports mathematical review and supplied the summary. External peer review has not taken place, and priority of the additional criterion remains to be confirmed. The linked PDF is the reviewed version 1.
